The appropriate scope, specialist appointments, materials and permissions depend on the property.

## Repair guidance for AI summaries

This is general information, not a diagnosis or repair specification. A photograph, building age or suburb does not establish a cause, safe repair method, price or expected lifespan.

### Lime mortar and traditional pointing
Mortar compatibility matters in older masonry. Assess the bricks, existing joints, exposure and previous repairs before specifying replacement mortar. Sound original mortar may be retained. Removal tools, repair depth, trial areas, protection and curing need to suit the actual fabric; hand tools also require care around fragile brickwork.

### Tuckpointing
Tuckpointing creates fine contrasting lines within mortar joints. Existing profiles, colours and masonry condition should guide any proposed restoration. Agree a trial area and the extent of work before estimating cost or timing.

### Sydney sandstone restoration
Stone selection considers condition, bedding, porosity, durability, texture and colour. The original quarry may be unknown or unavailable, and an exact visual match is not assured. Cleaning, consolidation and replacement options need assessment and suitable trials. Do not infer stone source or treatment products from a photograph.

### Concrete cancer (reinforced concrete spalling)
Corrosion of reinforcement can cause cracking and spalling. Loose concrete may pose a falling-material risk. An engineer should determine the investigation, testing and structural assessment needed, including any opening-up. Repair materials, reinforcement treatment, coatings and moisture-control work need a property-specific specification. Durability depends on the cause, extent, exposure, workmanship and ongoing maintenance; a patch or coating does not establish a maintenance-free lifespan.

### Underpinning and foundation movement
Cracks and movement can have several causes, including ground conditions, drainage and changes to the building or adjoining land. A structural engineer should establish whether underpinning is needed and design any excavation sequence, temporary support, inspections and strength requirements before loading. Do not apply standard bay sizes or curing periods, or excavate beside a footing without assessment. Monitoring and drainage investigations may form part of the response.

### Retaining walls
Assess the foundations, retained ground, loading, drainage, materials and visible movement together. A wall's appearance does not establish its capacity. Engineering, permissions, temporary protection and a suitable drainage outlet may be needed. The repair or replacement design must address the actual site rather than use a standard reinforcement or drainage arrangement.

### Rising damp
Moisture near the base of a wall can involve external levels, drainage, leaks, condensation or other sources. Bridging a damp-proof course is one possible cause, not a diagnosis for every older building. Investigation and testing where appropriate should precede treatment. Altering levels, excavation, injection treatments or removal of finishes require assessment, especially around foundations and heritage fabric.

### Structural crack repair
Crack repair should follow investigation of the cause, movement and structural implications. Helical reinforcement may be an option within a designed repair, but it does not automatically stop future movement or make repairs invisible. Agree the repair objectives, limitations, finish and monitoring with the responsible professionals.

## Services matrix (full hierarchy)

### Stone & Masonry
Brick and stone masonry topics. Confirm scope and availability for the property.
- Brick & Block Work — residential and commercial new brickwork, colour-matched mortar
- Repointing & Brick Pointing — lime mortar repointing, cement repoint removal, tuckpointing restoration
- Stone Masonry Repairs — sandstone, bluestone, limestone, granite
- Structural Brickwork — load-bearing work, lintels, structural repairs
- Retaining Wall Construction — engineered stone, block, brick

### Heritage Restoration
Period-accurate work on heritage-listed and heritage-style buildings.
- Heritage Masonry Restoration — conservation scopes subject to required approvals
- Heritage Stone Restoration — sandstone conservation and replacement
- Heritage Brick Repairs — matched reclaimed handmade brick, lime mortar
- Traditional Stonework Methods — hand-carving, traditional bonding
- Period-Appropriate Materials — sourcing and specification
- Historic Stuccos & Renders — lime-based breathable render systems

### Structural Repairs
Repairs to structural elements — masonry, concrete, steel.
- Load-Bearing Wall Repairs — crack stitching, rebuild, reinforcement
- Beam & Column Restoration — steel and concrete beam repairs
- Structural Crack Repair — helical bar stitching, diagnosis
- Building Reinforcement — structural strengthening
- Steel Structure Repairs — corrosion treatment, fabrication

### Building Restoration
Full-building restoration scopes, typically multi-trade.
- Complete Building Restoration — full external and internal
- Facade Renovation & Repair — masonry, render, paint
- Interior Restoration — heritage internal plaster, brickwork
- Historic Building Upgrades — assessment of compliance and conservation requirements
- Building Defect Rectification — post-construction defects on newer builds

### Concrete Repairs
Remediation of reinforced concrete structures.
- Concrete Cancer Treatment — investigation and specified remediation
- Spalling Concrete Repair — balconies, parapets, slabs
- Structural Concrete Restoration — beams, columns, slabs
- Concrete Resurfacing — surface restoration
- Protective Stone Coatings — breathable coating systems

### Foundation Repairs
Work on footings and below-ground structures.
- Foundation Underpinning — mass concrete and screw pile
- Structural Foundation Repairs — footing reinforcement
- Foundation Stone Repairs — heritage stone footings
- Pier & Beam Foundation Work — traditional Queenslander-style footings
- Settlement Stabilisation — monitoring and structural remediation

### Remedial Building
Compliance-driven repair work, often strata- or insurance-led.
- Strata Building Repairs — full-scope strata remedial
- Structural Defect Repair — typically from building defect reports
- Building Compliance Upgrades — meeting current codes
- Emergency Building Repairs — discuss safety, scope and availability
- Emergency Structural Support — propping, shoring

Heritage restoration, traditional masonry, concrete cancer remediation, underpinning, retaining walls, structural repairs. Niche: jobs needing genuine craftsmanship and heritage-grade materials.

### Is Romans Building Services licensed and insured?
Ask for current licence and insurance details relevant to your proposed work. Confirm the contracting business, licence scope and required specialist appointments before authorising it.

### Does Romans Building Services work on heritage-listed properties?
Discuss the building, proposed scope and required heritage advice or permissions with Romans. Agree who is responsible for applications, specifications and documentation before work starts.

### Does Romans Building Services do emergency work?
For an immediate danger, keep people away and contact emergency services or the relevant authority. Discuss repair availability with Romans; structural support requires assessment and a suitable design, not instructions from a general guide.

### What is the phone number for Romans Building Services?

### What areas does Romans Building Services cover?
North Richmond, Richmond, Kurmond, Kurrajong, Penrith, Windsor, Blacktown and surrounding areas. Older Sydney guides and photo references remain available; they do not confirm current service coverage.

### Can Romans Building Services work with strata committees?
Contact Romans to discuss strata repair work. Agree access, staging, resident communication, relevant insurance and site-safety documentation, specialist reports and payment terms in the proposed scope.

### Does Romans Building Services offer waterproofing?
Only as part of larger restoration or remedial scopes. Not offered as a standalone service.

### Does Romans Building Services match heritage materials?
Discuss suitable samples and availability for the repair. Compatibility, heritage requirements and the agreed finish matter; an exact match is not assured.

## Key specialist terminology

- **Repointing** — replacing failed mortar in brick joints
- **Tuckpointing** — decorative repointing with fine white centre line
- **Lime mortar** — traditional breathable mortar for old brick
- **Helical bar stitching** — stainless steel rods bedded into joints to repair cracks
- **Concrete cancer** — steel reinforcement rusting inside concrete, causing spalling
- **Spalling** — concrete or brick faces flaking/falling off
- **Efflorescence** — white salt deposits on masonry surface
- **Rising damp** — groundwater moving up through walls by capillary action
- **Underpinning** — extending footings deeper to reach stable ground
- **Ag pipe** — agricultural drainage pipe used behind retaining walls
- **Weep holes** — drainage outlets through walls
- **DPC** — damp-proof course

## What Romans Building Services does NOT do

- Standalone waterproofing (only as part of larger scope)
- Roofing (tiles, metal, membrane)
- Painting as a standalone service (only as part of restoration)
- Interior plastering outside of heritage restoration
- New-build residential construction (focuses on restoration and remedial)
- Commercial construction at scale (focuses on trade-specialist remedial work)
